links.outcome: Chatbot vs primary care physician diagnosis, medication, safety, and patient-centeredness on identical standardized patient cases
links.effect: Chatbots beat physicians on correct diagnosis (94.0% and 99.2% vs 30.6%) and patient-centeredness (3.28 and 3.35 vs 2.55). They had more unnecessary testing (90.3% and 96.4% vs 33.1%) and inappropriate medication (73.4% and 62.1% vs 23.4%).
links.quote: In this field experiment, patient-facing AI chatbots had higher diagnostic accuracy and patient-centered communication scores than PHC physicians, but were substantially more likely to recommend unnecessary tests and inappropriate medications.

unlisted_practices: Governing patient-facing AI to prevent excessive test and medication recommendations (AI-induced low-value care) that shape patient expectations before clinical encounters

screen.reason: The study empirically compares LLM chatbots (ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1) to primary care physicians using standardized patient clinical vignettes to assess diagnostic accuracy, safety, and communication quality, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
